summary: A waitlist you own: one HTML snippet pasted into any landing page posts emails to your server, each signup gets a position and a personal referral link that moves them up the queue, bots are turned away, and an admin page shows growth and exports CSV. No third-party service holds your list.

stack.why: a signup is one INSERT; a framework would outweigh the app
one file, transactional, easy to back up and export
works pasted into any page with JavaScript disabled
the snippet needs a public HTTPS endpoint

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: The landing page you will paste the form into
prerequisites.why: Phase 4 is tested by pasting the snippet into a real page on a different origin, so you need one to paste into.
prerequisites.get: Any page you control: your site, a Carrd, a Notion page with an embed, or a blank HTML file served locally is enough to start.

prerequisites.name: A disposable-email domain list
prerequisites.why: Phase 1 rejects throwaway addresses. A maintained list saves you writing one.
prerequisites.get: Download the domains file from the disposable-email-domains project on GitHub into your repo as data/disposable.txt.

prerequisites.name: A random salt for hashing IPs
prerequisites.why: You store a salted hash of the signer's IP for rate limiting, never the raw address.
prerequisites.get: Generate once with openssl rand -hex 32 and put it in .env as IP_SALT. Changing it later resets the rate limiter, nothing else.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: The snippet posts to this address from every page it lives on.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: PORT
env.where: Any free port; Caddy proxies to it.

env.name: DATABASE_PATH
env.where: SQLite file. Back it up; it is the list.

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Public base URL, used in referral links.

env.name: ALLOWED_ORIGINS
env.where: Comma-separated origins allowed to post the form. Anything else is refused.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: Signup and storage
phases.goal: Accept an email, normalise it, store it once, and treat a repeat signup as a lost tab rather than an attack.

steps.do: Create the project and the signups table
steps.detail: signups (id, email unique, created_at, referral_code unique, referred_by, confirmed, ip_hash, user_agent). Emails stored lowercased and trimmed.
commands: mkdir waitlist && cd waitlist && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Implement POST /api/waitlist
steps.detail: Accept form-encoded and JSON. Normalise, validate with one conservative regex and a 254-character cap, reject domains in data/disposable.txt.

steps.do: Make duplicates a friendly no-op
steps.detail: Insert inside a transaction. On a unique conflict, return the existing row's position rather than an error, because a double submit is a user who lost the tab.

steps.do: Mint the referral code on insert
steps.detail: Eight characters from an alphabet without 0/O/1/l/I, from crypto.randomBytes, retried on collision.

check: The same email posted twice yields one row and two identical responses
A malformed address is rejected with a readable message
An address at a disposable domain is rejected
Two concurrent posts of one new email still leave exactly one row
traps: Wrap the insert in a transaction. Without it a fast double click can mint two referral codes for one person.

phases.title: Referral mechanics
phases.goal: Referrals move people up the queue by exactly REFERRAL_BOOST places each, computed in one query so it stays fast at ten thousand signups.

steps.do: Resolve ?ref=CODE on signup
steps.detail: Set referred_by only if the code exists, is not the signer's own, and the pair is not already recorded. Unknown or self codes are ignored silently.

steps.do: Compute position in SQL
steps.detail: position = rank by created_at minus REFERRAL_BOOST times that signup's confirmed referrals, floored at 1. One query with a window function or a correlated count. Never a loop in application code.

steps.do: Return position and referral link from the signup endpoint
steps.detail: The link is SITE_URL plus ?ref=CODE. Also expose GET /api/position?code= so a returning signer can check.

check: Three people signing up through one link move that person up exactly 15 places (with the default boost)
A self-referral is ignored
An unknown ref code is ignored without an error
Positions are unique and gap-free when nobody has referred anyone

phases.title: Abuse controls
phases.goal: Stop the bots a public form attracts without ever refusing a real person.

steps.do: Add a CSS-hidden honeypot field
steps.detail: A text input named website, hidden with CSS (not type=hidden). Filled means: return the normal success screen, store nothing.

steps.do: Require a minimum fill time
steps.detail: A signed timestamp in a hidden field; submissions under 2 seconds old are rejected. Sign it with IP_SALT so it cannot be forged.

steps.do: Rate limit per IP in SQLite
steps.detail: 5 per hour and 20 per day keyed by ip_hash, stored in a table so it survives a restart.

steps.do: Cap the body and check the Origin header
steps.detail: 4 KB body cap. Refuse any Origin not in ALLOWED_ORIGINS with 403.

check: A filled honeypot returns success and writes no row
A sub-2-second submission is rejected
The sixth signup from one IP in an hour is refused while a different IP succeeds
A post from an origin not in the allowlist gets 403

phases.title: Public surface
phases.goal: The paste-in snippet and the confirmation screen with a working referral link.

steps.do: Write the snippet
steps.detail: One block of HTML: a form posting to SITE_URL/api/waitlist with email, the honeypot and the timestamp field. No script tag required. Styled with inherit so it takes the host page's font.

steps.do: Add the CORS headers the cross-origin post needs
steps.detail: Access-Control-Allow-Origin for origins in ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and handle the OPTIONS preflight.

steps.do: Build the confirmation page
steps.detail: Position, the personal referral link with a copy button, and share links for X, WhatsApp and email with the link pre-filled.

check: The snippet works pasted into a blank HTML file served on another port
The confirmation shows the correct position
The copy button puts a working link on the clipboard
Everything works with JavaScript disabled except the copy button

phases.title: Admin
phases.goal: See growth, find people, export, delete.

steps.do: Basic-auth /admin with the total and a signups-per-day bar chart as inline SVG
steps.detail: The chart is a GROUP BY on the date of created_at; no chart library.

steps.do: Add the top-referrers table and a searchable list with delete
steps.detail: Deleting a referrer must leave their referees' rows intact: null out referred_by rather than cascading.

steps.do: Stream a CSV export
steps.detail: Write rows as you read them; do not build the whole file in memory.

check: The chart matches a GROUP BY date query
A 10,000-row export opens in a spreadsheet and the process memory does not grow
Deleting a referrer leaves the people they referred in place

phases.title: Deploy and document
phases.goal: Live on your domain, embedded on your real landing page, documented.

steps.do: Install on the VPS with systemd and Caddy
commands: sudo cp deploy/waitlist.service /etc/systemd/system/ && sudo systemctl enable --now waitlist

steps.do: Add /healthz and a nightly SQLite backup command
Paste the snippet into the real landing page and write the README
steps.detail: README: the snippet verbatim, the exact referral maths, the ALLOWED_ORIGINS step, and one line stating no email is ever sent by this system.

check: A signup from the real landing page appears in /admin
A reader goes from clone to a live embedded form using only the README
The README states that no email is sent

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the signup endpoint is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.

steps.do: Lock the box down
steps.detail: Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A waitlist service you could run for several launches: one endpoint per origin list, referral maths that holds at scale, and a list you can export into any sender.

architecture.swap: Any handler producing the same signups rows
One SQL statement; change the boost or the rule here only

architecture.owns: the snippet, CORS and the confirmation page
architecture.swap: A JavaScript widget could replace the plain form without touching intake
Any UI over the same table

operations.backup: SQLite .backup nightly, off the box, thirty days kept. The list is the whole asset.
operations.restore: Copy the backup to DATABASE_PATH, start, confirm the total in /admin matches the last known count.
operations.monitoring: Uptime check on /healthz; alert if signups per day drops to zero during a campaign (a broken snippet looks exactly like no interest).
operations.incident: If a bot flood gets through: export, dedupe by ip_hash and timestamp pattern, delete the burst, tighten the rate limit. If IP_SALT leaks, rotate it; it only affects rate limiting.

releaseGate: A clean clone reaches an embedded form using only the README
Referral positions verified against a hand calculation on a seeded fixture of 1,000 signups
One restore drill performed and dated
The CSV imports cleanly into the email tool you intend to use

notIncluded: Sending email: no welcome mail, no blasts, no confirmation link. Deliverability is a whole product; export the CSV into a real sender.
Spam filtering beyond a honeypot and rate limits: this stops bots, not a determined human.
after: Double opt-in via a transactional email provider, behind an interface so the sender is swappable
A public counter widget showing total signups
